newsitem.title: DUBAI: SAA lifts cargo rates as rand weak/fuel up.
newsitem.headline: SAA lifts cargo rates as rand weak/fuel up.

text.p: The depreciation of the rand by more than 25 percent against the dollar since mid-February, coupled with higher jet fuel prices has prompted South African Airways Cargo to increase freight rates by as much as 20 percent, cargo marketing manager Willie Swart said.

"The rand going down has had a major effect on our operating costs," Swart, who is responsible for cargo marketing in the Americas, Middle East and Far East, told Reuters at the Air Cargo Forum in Dubai.

"Another possible shock looms ahead for the industry as jet fuel prices have increased by 37 percent year on year based on North West European prices and 49 percent based on the (domestic) South African jet fuel price," SAA said in a statement issued here separately on Wednesday.

"Due to extreme competition, it is unlikely that price increases of such magnitude will be passed on the consumer. This can only mean the industry is in for a period of rationalisation", SAA Cargo excutive manager, Charles Fairweather said in the statement.

Swart said rates into Africa had been raised 20 percent, those to Europe went up 10 percent and those to South America and Australia had been put up five percent. All increases were effective from October one, except the African ones which were introduced on August 1. Rates to the Far East had been left unchanged.
"There was no increases to the USA and we had fairly high yields and we could sustain existing rates," Swart said.
Heightened competition since the start of the political reform process in 1990 has limited SAA Cargo's room for rate increases.
"Since 1990 the number of scheduled operators through Johannesburg has increased from about 12 to 54," he said.
"We have held on to volume and increased it, but maybe we've lost a bit of the market share in percentage terms, but the market has grown," he added.
Asked if he expected any more increases, Swart said: "We have nothing planned at this stage. We are trying to increase productivity."
After rising two and half times since 1992, SAA Cargo expects turnover of 900 million rand ($197.9 million) in the year to end-March 1997 with volumes of 346,000 tonnes.

A separate unit of South African Airways, the cargo division owns four freighters -- a Boeing 747-200, two 737s and an Airbus 300. It leases another 747-200 and operates three 747s in a joint venture with Lufthansa LHAG.FA. ($ = 4.547 South African Rand)
